{{Quote|One of the Emperor's advisors, one Crueya Vandron, saw the potential wealth of a populist movement which could be molded into a political tool.|[[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]]|<ref name="imp" />}}
'''Crueya Vandron''' was the [[Lord/Legends|lord]] of [[House Vandron]], one of the Ancient Houses of the [[Senex sector/Legends|Senex sector]]; additionally, he was an advisor to [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], and an important figure in the establishment of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]]. Alongside his wife, Lady [[Theala Vandron]], he ruled the Senex [[Sector/Legends|sector]], an ancient domain that operated independently from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

After the Senex sector finally joined the Republic during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], Vandron became an advisor to Chancellor Palpatine and a leading member of the [[Commission for the Protection of the Republic/Legends|Commission for the Protection of the Republic]]. When Palpatine dissolved the Republic and created the first [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Vandron helped shape the [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|Commission for the Preservation of the New Order]]&mdash;COMPOR's successor&mdash;into a driving force in Imperial organization, alongside the likes of [[Ishin-Il-Raz]], [[Ardus Kaine]], and [[Janus Greejatus/Legends|Janus Greejatus]]. While he was not a member of the organization personally, he provided the funding for much of its activities, and he also helped establish the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]]; a [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentrist]] and a deep believer in the Empire and its key ideals, he attempted to work the idea of "Imperial infallibility" into the Imperial legal code around [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], but was met with stern opposition by the [[Coalition for Progress/Legends#Justice|Justice]] department. By [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], [[Theala Vandron Jr.]] had assumed the leadership of House Vandron.

==Biography==
===Lord Vandron===
{{Quote|On behalf of Lord Crueya and Lady Theala of House Vandron, it is our honor to welcome you to the Senex sector.|House Vandron representative, to a group of Jedi|<ref name="cod" />}}
Crueya Vandron was born into nobility in the [[Senex sector/Legends|Senex sector]] during the waning years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. He was a member of [[House Vandron]],<ref name="cod" /> thought to be the oldest and most noble of the Ancient Houses of [[Senex-Juvex/Legends|Senex-Juvex]].<ref name="cotj" /> Vandron eventually became an influential and powerful [[Lord/Legends|lord]], and married Lady [[Theala Vandron]]. The Senex [[Sector/Legends|sector]] was an aristocracy that operated outside of the Republic, and had its own distinct laws and customs; they bred [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], which was against the ideals of the Republic. Because of this, the Republic&mdash;under [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]]&mdash;refused to openly trade with Crueya Vandron and his fellow lords, despite the urgings of the Senex sector's inhabitants.<ref name="cod" />

In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], members of the [[Nebula Front/Legends|Nebula Front]] militant group seized control of one of the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] under the rule of House Vandron, [[Asmeru/Legends|Asmeru]], from the few natives who inhabited it; as Vandron and his fellow lords did not want to become prey to the Front's attacks, they allowed them to operate out of Asmeru without interference. After a fruitless attempt to [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] Chancellor Valorum that year, Nebula Front members led by [[Arwen Cohl]] fled to Asmeru; the houses of the Senex sector, and Crueya Vandron in particular, came under immense pressure from the Republic, who accused them of granting the terrorists safe haven. Knowing that cooperation with the Republic might persuade Valorum to grant the sector trading rights, Vandron and his counterpart in [[House Elegin/Legends|House Elegin]] denied the accusations, but offered to help Republic forces keep the Nebula Front resistance fighters on Asmeru while the [[Eriadu Trade Summit]] took place, to prevent the terrorists from interfering there.<ref name="cod" />

Although the Republic was wary of working alongside slavers, they accepted Vandron's offer, sending two [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class cruisers]] and a team of thirty [[Judicial Department/Legends|Judicials]] and several [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. During the mission, one of the cruisers was fired upon, though it was never learned who by; many, such as [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bail Antilles/Legends|Bail Antilles]], suspected House Vandron was responsible, but Vandron publicly denied this. On the surface of Asmeru, the team of Jedi overstepped their bounds and attacked natives; Vandron used this as a bargaining chip against the Republic: he agreed to let the incident pass without formally objecting to the Jedi's actions in exchange for the trading rights the Senex sector so craved. With little other option, Valorum agreed to overlook their practices regarding slavery and granted them free trading with Republic states.<ref name="cod" />

===Advisor Vandron===
{{Quote|This is sensationalist nonsense. These echelons that gathered today mark the first generation of the SAGroup brigadiers. We cannot help that the first to join happened to be of human descent. We have non-human applicants, to be sure. Their applications are still under review.|Crueya Vandron, addressing concerns about COMPOR's Humanocentrism to the media|<ref name="core" />}}
[[File:70RepublicYouthSpeechFinal.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A COMPOR rally.]]
Eventually, sometime between the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Blockade]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] and the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the Senex sector joined the Galactic Republic, at the urging of [[Terr Taneel/Legends|Terr Taneel]], who became its first [[Senator/Legends|senator]].<ref name="ttdb">{{DB|character|terrtaneel|Taneel, Terr}}</ref> Crueya Vandron became a close advisor to Chancellor [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], Valorum's successor. He became interested in COMPOR&mdash;the [[Commission for the Protection of the Republic/Legends|Commission for the Protection of the Republic]]&mdash;which was little more than a social gathering for fanatic supporters of the Republic;<ref name="core" /> Vandron, however, saw the potential to mold it into a propaganda machine.<ref name="imp" /> The Senex lord was appointed to monitor the group and provide it with resources.<ref name="inaug">{{InsiderCite|84|Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241}}</ref>

Midway during the Clone Wars, [[SAGroup (COMPOR)/Legends|SAGroup]], a sub-organization of COMPOR composed entirely of youths, held a massive rally in [[Monument Plaza/Legends|Monument Plaza]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], which garnered the attention of much of the Republic, particularly its media. However, while the rally itself was not criticized, many echelons of the media disapproved of what they viewed as [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] tendencies in SAGroup; of its three thousand members, more than 95% were [[Human/Legends|Human]], and those select few [[Non-huMan|non-Humans]] were all of [[near-Human]] descent. Vandron attempted to address these concerns, telling [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] reporters that this was merely coincidence and that they had had many non-Human applicants, though none had been admitted.<ref name="core" />

===The New Order===
{{Quote|Advisor Vandron is in full support of our mission and has made a commitment to growing COMPNOR.|Ishin-Il-Raz|<ref name="inaug" />}}
In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Chancellor Palpatine, with the support of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], dissolved the Republic and reformed it as the first [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], named himself as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], and established the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]].<ref name="rots">{{Film|III}}</ref> Crueya Vandron retained his post as advisor, and again was tasked with making COMPOR&mdash;which had since been reformed as the [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|Commission for the Preservation of the New Order]] in one of Palpatine's first acts as Emperor&mdash;into a tool and a weapon for Palpatine to wield. Vandron corresponded with [[Ishin-Il-Raz]], head of COMPNOR's [[Select Committee/Legends|Select Committee]], as to what path the organization would take; Vandron approved, and agreed to fund expansions to the Committee.<ref name="inaug" />

[[File:Rally.jpg|thumb|right|205px|Ishin-Il-Raz, at COMPNOR's opening rally.]]
However, COMPNOR was still little more than a social club for rich, Human patriots, and few regarded it as something that would make an impact on [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Vandron, however, saw potential to make it just that; although he was not officially a member of COMPNOR's Select Committee, with the backing of Emperor Palpatine he began to mold the organization as he saw fit.<ref name="imp" />

COMPNOR still had many prominent members who were wary of Palpatine and how COMPOR had been reorganized and reshuffled, and Vandron sought to weed them out before building the organization any further. With Palpatine's aid, he removed them, one by one, not through public opposition but through guile and intrigue; eventually, Vandron and the Emperor had the opponents of COMPNOR's change wondering what exactly was different between COMPNOR as it was and how they envisioned it through a series of shrewd moves, and opposition slowly died down. Vandron provided the funding<ref name="imp" /> for the likes of Il-Raz,<ref name="nec">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> [[Janus Greejatus/Legends|Janus Greejatus]],<ref name="jgdb">{{DB|character|janusgreejatus|Greejatus, Janus}}</ref> and [[Ardus Kaine]]<ref name="aj">{{JournalCite|3|The Pentastar Alignment}}</ref> to shape COMPNOR, and many sub-organizations were formed to ensure every part of the Empire was being checked over. Vandron had no official capacity within the organization, but each change or new group the Select Committee wanted to form had to go through him, and by extension the Emperor, for approval. During the period between 19 BBY and the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], Vandron helped form the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] to keep tabs on<ref name="imp" /> [[Armand Isard/Legends|Armand Isard's]]<ref name="iad">{{StoryCite|story=Interlude at Darkknell|book=Tales from the New Republic}}</ref> [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]].<ref name="imp" />

COMPNOR was not without its faults, though, and it constantly feuded with Imperial Intelligence; some, such as Ardus Kaine, saw this as a huge waste of time and resources and ceased having any part in COMPNOR because of it.<ref name="aj" /> Several years before the Battle of [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin]], the Emperor began to have many Imperial diplomats and senators whom he did not trust killed. As a way to show the galaxy's citizens that he was a benevolent and kind leader, Palpatine spoke with the children of each of the murdered delegates, telling them their parents had been killed by anti-Imperial terrorists; the children became famous on Coruscant, and in an attempt to hold them up as an example of all, Vandron insisted that the children be drafted into the newly reformed [[Sub-Adult Group/Legends|SAGroup]], where they were given a vast education, with [[Imperial Military/Legends|military]] operations, bureaucracy, and intelligence being the foremost subjects on the curriculum. Vandron's idea was at least partially unsuccessful, as one of the children, [[Kerri Lessev/Legends|Kerri Lessev]], became a top agent of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="cro">''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]''</ref>

Some years later, Vandron attempted to work "Imperial infallibility" into the Empire's legal code, but was met with great resistance from the [[Coalition for Progress/Legends#Justice|Justice]] department; he had Imperial Security agents harass his opponents, and had many of them replaced with those whose loyalty he was sure of.<ref name="imp" /> By [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], Vandron had been replaced by [[Theala Vandron Jr.]] as the head of House Vandron.<ref name="cotj" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Recently, Crueya Vandron has been trying to work the idea of 'Imperial infallibility' into the code.|Voren Na'al, commenting on Vandron's idolizing of the Empire|<ref name="imp" />}}
Crueya Vandron was an unscrupulous man, who cared little for other beings. In his native Senex sector, he funded the "growing" of slaves, and refused to cease doing so even at the urging of the Republic. Thus, the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] saw Vandron and his peers as immoral, and were reluctant to work with them during the crisis involving the Nebula Front. Vandron knew how to turn things to his advantage, and was not above using methods such as blackmail to put himself where he wanted to be.<ref name="cod" /> Vandron was a believer in [[High Human Culture/Legends|Human High Culture]]<ref name="core" /> and in the ideals of the New Order; loyal to a fault, he gave up his lofty position in the Senex system to work for Chancellor Palpatine. Vandron believed in the Imperial way, and considered Palpatine's Empire infallible.<ref name="imp" />

==Behind the scenes==
Crueya Vandron was first mentioned in [[Greg Gorden]]'s [[1989]] ''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]'', and later in ''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]'' and the second edition of the ''Imperial Sourcebook''. In [[1995]], [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']] by [[Barbara Hambly]] featured an aristocratic "House Vandron," though Crueya Vandron was never linked to it. In [[2001]], over a decade after his creation, [[James Luceno]] featured Vandron in a minor role in his novel ''[[Cloak of Deception]]'', which was the first source to link the character to House Vandron. Several years later, [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Pablo Hidalgo]] made reference to the character in the [[Republic HoloNet News Core Edition 14:9:04|''Republic HoloNet News Core Edition'']] and [[Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241|''Special Inaugural Edition'']].
